finding.claim: SQL injection in ORDER BY: the $_GET['sort'] value is concatenated unescaped into the query. An attacker can use subqueries or CASE expressions for blind data extraction from any table, including boolean/time-based exfiltration. Stacked queries are unlikely with SQLite query(), but data disclosure still applies.
finding.sink: $pdo->query("SELECT id, name FROM users ORDER BY " . $sort)

trace.note: concatenated into SQL string and executed via PDO::query

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, cast, or quoting on this path. Contrast list_users_safe (line 10-11) which uses an allowlist map, and find_user (line 16) which uses a prepared statement; both are safe and not reported. No authentication or authorization checks exist in the file.

verdict.reason: list.php:5-6 takes $_GET['sort'] and concatenates it unvalidated into the ORDER BY query run via $pdo->query, and the file has no auth or allowlist on this path (the allowlist at list.php:10-11 only protects list_users_safe).
